advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the `install-unlocked` fallback creates/activates a venv (or document the venv step) so the uv-less path cannot pip-install into system Python.
evidence: Old flow (diff): `uv venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate     # or: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` then `make install`
New TL;DR — docs/local-dev-env.md:18-23: `make install` first, then `source .venv/bin/activate` (no venv-creation step)

Makefile:49-51 `install-unlocked:` runs `python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'` with no venv creation/activation — the Makefile error path steers uv-less users here: Makefile:44 `Unlocked fallback (resolves fresh — NOT the canonical env): make install-unlocked`
advisory.finding: The docs TL;DR dropped the explicit `uv venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` (or `python -m venv`) step that previously preceded `make install`. This is fine for the uv `uv sync` path (uv creates .venv), but the documented `install-unlocked` fallback runs `python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'` with no venv guaranteed — a user without uv who takes the fallback can pip-install rebar+dev deps into their global/system Python.
scenarios: A contributor without uv runs `make install`, sees the uv-required error, runs `make install-unlocked` from a shell with no activated venv, and pip installs into the system interpreter.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either restore a `python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` line before the fallback in docs, or have the `install-unlocked` target create/target a `.venv` explicitly (e.g. `python -m venv .venv && ./.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'`).
